test_cases.scenario: Unauthenticated user is redirected from the Programmes page
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the Programmes page URL without being logged in.
test_cases.expected: The browser redirects to the login page. The Programmes list is not shown.

test_cases.scenario: User with view-only access can see the Programmes list but no management actions
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user without management permissions.
2. Navigate to Projects > Programmes.
test_cases.expected: The Programmes list is visible. No Edit, Toggle, or Delete actions appear on any row. Add Programme, Import, and Export buttons are not shown.

test_cases.scenario: User with 'can_change_programme' sees Edit and Toggle actions
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with 'can_change_programme' permission.
2. Navigate to Projects > Programmes.
3. Expand a non-protected row's action menu.
test_cases.expected: Edit and Toggle (activate/deactivate) actions are visible and enabled for non-protected programmes.

test_cases.scenario: User with 'can_delete_programme' sees the Delete action for non-protected programmes
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in as a user with 'can_delete_programme' permission.
2. Navigate to Projects > Programmes.
3. Expand a non-protected row's action menu.
test_cases.expected: A Delete action (danger-styled) is visible for non-protected programmes.

test_cases.scenario: Add Programme, Import, and Export buttons are visible in the page header
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects > Programmes.
2. Check the page header.
test_cases.expected: Add Programme, Import, and Export buttons are visible after the page loads.

test_cases.scenario: Programmes page loads with the correct layout and table
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Projects > Programmes.
test_cases.expected: The page shows the 'Projects' eyebrow, 'Programmes' heading, and subtitle 'Manage programmes that group and govern projects across your organisation.' The table shows: Programme Name, Code, Description, Status, Created columns.

test_cases.scenario: Default filter shows only active programmes
test_cases.steps:
1. Navigate to Projects > Programmes.
2. Check the Is Active filter.
test_cases.expected: Is Active defaults to 'Active'. Only active programmes are listed.

test_cases.scenario: Search by name filters the list
test_cases.steps: 1. Type a programme name in the search field.
test_cases.expected: Only programmes whose names match the search term are shown.

test_cases.scenario: Is Active filter set to 'All' shows both active and inactive programmes
test_cases.steps: 1. Change Is Active to 'All'.
test_cases.expected: Both active and inactive programmes appear in the table.

test_cases.scenario: Table can be sorted by Programme Name column
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the 'Programme Name' column header.
test_cases.expected: Rows sort alphabetically by name. A second click reverses the order.

test_cases.scenario: Table can be sorted by Created date column
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the 'Created' column header.
test_cases.expected: Rows sort by creation date. A second click reverses the order.

test_cases.scenario: Pressing '/' focuses the search field
test_cases.steps: 1. Press '/' on the keyboard.
test_cases.expected: The search field receives focus.

test_cases.scenario: Empty state shown when no programmes match the search
test_cases.steps: 1. Search for a term that matches no programme.
test_cases.expected: 'No programmes found.' is shown in the table area.

test_cases.scenario: Pagination loads more programmes when the list exceeds 25
test_cases.steps: 1. Set Is Active to 'All' and navigate to the next page if more than 25 exist.
test_cases.expected: Pagination controls appear. The next page loads correctly.

test_cases.scenario: Active filter chips appear below the filter panel
test_cases.steps: 1. Apply a search term.
test_cases.expected: An active filter chip appears below the filter panel. Removing it clears the filter.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Add Programme opens the create drawer
test_cases.steps: 1. Click 'Add Programme' in the page header.
test_cases.expected: The create programme drawer slides open with Programme Name and Description fields.

test_cases.scenario: Creating a programme with a valid name adds it to the list
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter a programme name (e.g., 'Digital Transformation').
3. Click 'Create programme'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. A success toast appears. The new programme is visible in the table as Active.

test_cases.scenario: Programme Name is required
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Leave the name blank.
3. Click 'Create programme'.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears on the Programme Name field. The drawer stays open and nothing is saved.

test_cases.scenario: Programme Name has a maximum length of 255 characters
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter more than 255 characters in the Programme Name field.
test_cases.expected: The character counter updates as the user types. The field enforces the 255-character limit.

test_cases.scenario: Character counter shows remaining characters as the user types the name
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Type into the Programme Name field.
test_cases.expected: A character counter displays the characters used (e.g., '21 / 255'). It updates on each keystroke.

test_cases.scenario: Description is optional — programme can be created without it
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter a name but leave Description blank.
3. Click 'Create programme'.
test_cases.expected: The programme is created successfully without a description.

test_cases.scenario: Description has a maximum length of 500 characters
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter more than 500 characters in the Description field.
test_cases.expected: The description field enforces the 500-character limit.

test_cases.scenario: Duplicate programme name is rejected
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter a name that already exists.
3. Click 'Create programme'.
test_cases.expected: An error toast or inline error indicates the name is already in use. No duplicate is created.

test_cases.scenario: Cancel button closes the create drawer without saving
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create drawer.
2. Enter some details.
3. Click 'Cancel'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. No programme is created.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking a programme row opens the view drawer
test_cases.steps: 1. Click anywhere on a programme row (not on an action button).
test_cases.expected: The view drawer slides open showing the selected programme's details.

test_cases.scenario: View drawer displays all expected fields
test_cases.steps: 1. Click a programme row to open the view drawer.
test_cases.expected: The view drawer shows: Programme Name, Code (monospace), Description, Status, Created (meta), and Created by (meta).

test_cases.scenario: View drawer shows 'Edit Programme' button for users with edit permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in with 'can_change_programme' permission.
2. Open the view drawer for a non-protected programme.
test_cases.expected: The view drawer footer shows an 'Edit Programme' button alongside the Close button.

test_cases.scenario: View drawer shows only Close button for users without edit permission
test_cases.steps:
1. Log in without 'can_change_programme' permission.
2. Open the view drawer for any programme.
test_cases.expected: Only the Close button appears in the footer. No 'Edit Programme' button is present.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking 'Edit Programme' in the view drawer opens the edit drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the view drawer for a non-protected programme.
2. Click 'Edit Programme' in the footer.
test_cases.expected: The view drawer closes and the edit drawer opens for the same programme, pre-populated with its current values.

test_cases.scenario: Close button dismisses the view drawer
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the view drawer.
2. Click 'Close'.
test_cases.expected: The view drawer slides closed. The list remains unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Code is shown in monospace style in the view drawer
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the view drawer for a programme.
test_cases.expected: The Code field is displayed in monospace, visually distinct from other text fields.

test_cases.scenario: Edit action opens the edit drawer pre-populated with the current name and description
test_cases.steps: 1. Click the Edit action on a non-protected programme.
test_cases.expected: The edit drawer opens with the Programme Name and Description pre-filled with the current values.

test_cases.scenario: Saving changes updates the programme in the list
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer for a programme.
2. Change the name and/or description.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. A success toast appears. The updated name and description are reflected in the table.

test_cases.scenario: Programme Name cannot be cleared in edit
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Clear the name.
3. Click 'Save changes'.
test_cases.expected: A validation error appears on the name field. The programme is not saved with an empty name.

test_cases.scenario: Cancel button in the edit drawer discards changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Change the name.
3. Click 'Cancel'.
test_cases.expected: The drawer closes. The programme name in the table is unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Character counter updates in the edit drawer as the user types
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the edit drawer.
2. Type in the Programme Name field.
test_cases.expected: The character counter updates in real time.

test_cases.scenario: Toggle action on an active programme opens a deactivation confirmation
test_cases.steps: 1. Click Toggle on an active, non-protected programme.
test_cases.expected: A deactivation confirmation modal appears.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deactivation sets the programme to Inactive
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Toggle on an active programme.
2. Confirm in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. A success toast appears. The Status column shows 'Inactive'.

test_cases.scenario: Toggle action on an inactive programme opens an activation confirmation
test_cases.steps:
1. Find an inactive programme (set Is Active to 'All').
2. Click Toggle on it.
test_cases.expected: An activation confirmation modal appears.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming activation sets the programme to Active
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Toggle on an inactive programme.
2. Confirm in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The Status column updates to 'Active'.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling the toggle confirmation makes no change
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Toggle on a programme.
2. Click Cancel in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The programme's status is unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Edit action is disabled for protected programmes
test_cases.steps:
1. Locate a protected programme in the list.
2. View its row actions.
test_cases.expected: The Edit action is visible but shown in a disabled state. It cannot be clicked.

test_cases.scenario: Toggle action is disabled for protected programmes
test_cases.steps:
1. Locate a protected programme.
2. View the Toggle action in its row.
test_cases.expected: The Toggle action is visible but disabled. Clicking it has no effect.

test_cases.scenario: Delete action is hidden for protected programmes
test_cases.steps:
1. Locate a protected programme.
2. Expand the row actions.
test_cases.expected: The Delete action is completely hidden for protected programmes — it does not appear at all, unlike the Edit and Toggle actions which are disabled.

test_cases.scenario: Non-protected programmes have all actions enabled
test_cases.steps:
1. Locate a non-protected programme.
2. Expand its row actions.
test_cases.expected: Edit, Toggle, and Delete actions are all enabled and interactive (subject to user permissions).

test_cases.scenario: Delete action opens a confirmation modal
test_cases.steps: 1. Click Delete on a non-protected programme.
test_cases.expected: A delete confirmation modal appears showing the programme name.

test_cases.scenario: Confirming deletion removes the programme from the list
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a non-protected programme.
2. Confirm in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. A success toast appears. The programme is removed from the table.

test_cases.scenario: Cancelling deletion makes no changes
test_cases.steps:
1. Click Delete on a programme.
2. Click Cancel in the modal.
test_cases.expected: The modal closes. The programme remains in the table unchanged.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Import opens the import panel
test_cases.steps: 1. Click 'Import' in the page header.
test_cases.expected: The import view opens allowing a file to be uploaded for importing programmes.

test_cases.scenario: Clicking Export opens the export panel
test_cases.steps: 1. Click 'Export' in the page header.
test_cases.expected: The export panel opens.

test_cases.scenario: Export respects the active filter
test_cases.steps:
1. Apply a search filter to narrow the list.
2. Click Export.
test_cases.expected: The exported file contains only programmes matching the current filter.

test_cases.scenario: Table refreshes after a successful import
test_cases.steps:
1. Import a valid programmes file.
2. Complete the import.
test_cases.expected: The table refreshes and newly imported programmes appear in the list.

test_cases.scenario: Page loads within an acceptable time
test_cases.steps: 1. Navigate to Projects > Programmes.
test_cases.expected: The page and table load within 3 seconds.

test_cases.scenario: Session expiry during an action redirects to login
test_cases.steps:
1. Open the create or edit drawer.
2. Let the session expire.
3. Attempt to save.
test_cases.expected: The browser redirects to the login page. No partial data is saved.

test_cases.scenario: Table refreshes automatically after create, edit, or delete
test_cases.steps: 1. Create, edit, or delete a programme.
test_cases.expected: The table updates to reflect the change without requiring a full page reload.

test_cases.scenario: All table columns are visible on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. Open Projects > Programmes on a desktop browser (1280px+ wide).
test_cases.expected: Programme Name, Code, Description, Status, and Created columns are all visible.

test_cases.scenario: View drawer fields appear in correct layout on desktop
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the view drawer for a programme on desktop.
test_cases.expected: Programme Name and Code appear side by side (col-md-6). Description spans full width. Status, Created, and Created by appear side by side.

test_cases.scenario: Row action buttons accessible on desktop without overflow menu
test_cases.steps: 1. Hover over a programme row on desktop.
test_cases.expected: Edit, Toggle, and Delete (where permitted) are accessible inline.

test_cases.scenario: Only Programme Name and Status columns visible in the table on mobile
test_cases.steps: 1. Open Projects > Programmes on a mobile device.
test_cases.expected: Only the Programme Name and Status columns are visible. Code, Description, and Created are hidden.

test_cases.scenario: Row actions accessible via overflow menu on mobile
test_cases.steps: 1. On mobile, tap the overflow menu on a programme row.
test_cases.expected: A menu appears with the available permitted actions.

test_cases.scenario: View and create drawers render correctly on mobile
test_cases.steps: 1. Open the view drawer and create drawer on a mobile device.
test_cases.expected: Both drawers render full-screen on mobile. Fields are readable and buttons are easy to tap.

test_cases.scenario: Newly created programme is available when assigning a programme to a project
test_cases.steps:
1. Create a new programme (e.g., 'Customer Experience').
2. Navigate to the Projects list and open or create a project.
3. Look for the Programme field.
test_cases.expected: The newly created 'Customer Experience' programme is available for selection on the project.

test_cases.scenario: Deactivating a programme removes it from the available selections in project forms
test_cases.steps:
1. Deactivate an existing programme.
2. Open a project to assign a programme.
3. Check the Programme dropdown.
test_cases.expected: The deactivated programme no longer appears in the Programme dropdown for projects.

test_cases.scenario: Projects already assigned to a deactivated programme retain the assignment
test_cases.steps:
1. Deactivate a programme that is already assigned to existing projects.
2. View one of those projects.
test_cases.expected: Existing projects retain their programme assignment. The deactivation only prevents future selection.

test_cases.scenario: Programme name change is reflected on assigned projects
test_cases.steps:
1. Edit a programme and change its name.
2. View a project assigned to that programme.
test_cases.expected: The project shows the updated programme name.
